clue.text: A comfortable place in the garden

definitions.text: A comfortable place in the garden

parts.words: A comfortable place in the garden
parts.note: a phrase for an easy, pleasant situation read literally as a flower bed planted with a favourite shrub

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a cosy spot to relax outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a life of ease is taken literally: a garden plot of the flowers it names.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an easy, pleasant situation, and literally it is a flower bed in a garden.

clue.text: Ruth left a noisy scene

parts.note: Babe Ruth was the famous American baseball player, so Ruth suggests his nickname Babe

explanation.surface: Ruth walked away from a loud, chaotic gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a woman's name, but it points to the baseball star Babe Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical tower gave its name to any confused uproar of voices.

clue.text: Make the expected contribution when Lorna's injured

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so Lorna's gives her surname with a possessive
bit means bitten, as when a dog has injured someone with its teeth

explanation.surface: Someone does their duty when a woman called Lorna gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of a classic English novel; the possessive gives DOONE'S, then BIT (bitten) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to play one's part or share in a joint effort.

clue.text: After a motion, peers defer kin's claim to property

indicators.note: a motion is movement, so the letters that follow are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Following a parliamentary motion, the nobles give way to a relative's claim on an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a motion' reads as parliamentary procedure, but it signals that PEERS DEFER KIN'S is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground saying asserts that whoever comes upon a lost item may keep it.

clue.text: Demanding love, emperor leads the country

indicators.note: leads says the emperor comes in front of the country in the answer

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, shown by the letter O
Nero was a Roman emperor
US is a common abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An emperor who demands love takes charge of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burdensome or taxing makes heavy demands on a person.

clue.text: A title makes me a lord

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of the following words are turned into something new

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that being given a rank of nobility turns them into a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' tells you to rearrange ME A LORD.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of a nobleman of that grade is a hereditary honour or style.

clue.text: Old part of Swanage destroyed

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient section of the Dorset seaside town was wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Swanage is a seaside town in Dorset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person or thing that has lived or existed a long time.

clue.text: Fresh information about the interior

indicators.note: the interior says one piece is placed within the other piece

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: New details are offered about the inside of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the interior' puts RE inside GEN; 'Fresh' is the definition, as in new or unripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Unripe or newly made things are described with this colour word, as in inexperienced recruits.

clue.text: Spread spare lids out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are disordered or set wrongly

explanation.surface: Someone scatters spare lids about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' tells you to rearrange SPARE LIDS; 'Spread' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattering or distribution of things over a wide area.

clue.text: Theatre — of war?

parts.note: a hospital theatre is where surgery happens, and a theatre of war is where military campaigns are directed from

explanation.surface: A question about whether a playhouse might be a battle zone.
explanation.walkthrough: A surgical theatre is where operations are carried out; the military sense is a headquarters from which campaigns are run.
explanation.definitionFit: A headquarters for directing military campaigns, also punning on a surgical theatre.

clue.text: Chocolate cake to have with cheese covering

indicators.note: covering says the cheese is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Someone eats a chocolate dessert topped with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense square of baked chocolate sponge is a popular American sweet.

clue.text: Make more records from master

definitions.meaning: to master feelings is to hold them down or subdue them

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing discs again is a fresh print run, and holding feelings in check is to suppress them.

clue.text: Tell tales, say, about my superior

parts.note: telling tales is fibbing, to lie

indicators.note: about signals that the word for say is turned round

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG
Lord! is an exclamation of surprise like My!

explanation.surface: Someone gossips about their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EG round to GE; 'my' is the exclamation, as in 'My Lord!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal lord is the master to whom a vassal owes allegiance.

clue.text: Wander about in the mountains

definitions.meaning: to roam freely over an area

explanation.definitionFit: Cattle roam freely over open land, and a line of peaks is called a chain.

clue.text: Board sends English doctor to America

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medical board posts a British physician across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends ... to' just places the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on a motor coach, the way one might board a train.

clue.text: Obtainable from there, a new girdle

indicators.note: obtainable from says the answer can be got by rearranging the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A new belt can be bought over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtainable from' tells you to rearrange THERE A NEW; 'girdle' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle with a garland of flowers is to ring something round.

clue.text: Occasionally see a few papers

parts.note: some means a few
The Times is a newspaper, and times here are copies of papers

explanation.surface: Someone browses a handful of newspapers now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TIMES is a British national newspaper, the one carrying this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and then, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Street-vendor makin' a mess of island

parts.note: muffin' is a dropped-g form of muffing, botching or making a mess of something
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A hawker bungles things on a small island.
explanation.walkthrough: The muffin man was a traditional London seller of muffins, remembered in a nursery rhyme; the Isle of Man is a British island.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller who went door to door with baked rolls on a tray.

clue.text: Saw Sweden — it's stirring

indicators.note: stirring signals that the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A remark that Sweden is exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the past tense of see; 'stirring' tells you to rearrange SWEDEN IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: To have observed or been present at an event.

clue.text: Con man turns up in disgrace

parts.note: to con is to study or examine closely, to scan

indicators.note: turns up signals that, in a down clue, the word for man is read upwards

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A swindler appears amid shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle but means to peruse; 'turns up' reverses LAD to DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Public shame or outrage caused by wrongdoing.

clue.text: Refuse to go in here and clean tip up

parts.note: to dust is to clean

indicators.note: up signals that, in a down clue, the word for tip is read upwards

parts.note: a nib is the tip of a pen

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to enter a house until it has been cleaned and tidied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish; 'up' turns NIB into BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for household rubbish.

clue.text: What's left of the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A question about what remains of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers' leftovers: the entrails and organs remaining once the meat is cut.

clue.text: The latest in style, Sally's outfit

indicators.note: the latest is the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally wears the newest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally is not a name but a witty remark; ''s' is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To outfit is to supply with the necessary gear.

clue.text: In Paris, a match is free

parts.note: un is French for a
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A football fixture in Paris costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British term for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen knots is to set loose.

clue.text: Fixing the value of grass given to donkeys

indicators.note: given to says the second piece is attached after the donkeys

parts.note: asses are donkeys
to grass is slang for informing to police, to sing

explanation.surface: Feeding hay to donkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for informing on someone, as is 'sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaluating or appraising something.

clue.text: Eat too much Cheddar, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Cheddar is a ravine in Somerset, an example of a steep valley

explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar looks like the cheese but is the Somerset ravine of that name, in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is stuffing oneself, and the Somerset ravine is a famous steep-sided valley.

clue.text: Instructed trade union to see the German revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary signals that the German word is turned round

parts.note: der is German for the

explanation.surface: Instructions to union members to meet a German radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns DER into RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Taught or coached privately.

clue.text: An error in 1 ac

definitions.meaning: something flowering would be found in the bed of roses at 1 across

explanation.definitionFit: A howler or gaffe, and a flowering plant such as one in a rose bed.

clue.text: Plane is still level

definitions.meaning: as in still more, a degree further

explanation.definitionFit: A flat surface, an intensifier as in yet better, and equal scores all describe this word.

clue.text: Mountain crest comprises hog's-back shape

parts.note: Mont Blanc is the Alps' highest peak

indicators.note: comprises says the crest piece holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a mane is the hair along a horse's crest

indicators.note: back means the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A ridge on a hill looks like the curved back of a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shape' is the moulded milk pudding; 'hog's-back' gives G, the last letter of hog.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulded pudding, set in a jelly mould, is often called a shape.
